ai.definition: MoE Architecture is a machine learning framework that combines multiple simpler models into an ensemble to improve overall performance and efficiency. Each component of the ensemble specializes in different parts of the problem space.
ai.howItWorks: Models within the MoE architecture are trained on specific tasks or subsets of data, allowing them to specialize. At inference time, a gating network selects which components should contribute based on the input characteristics, leading to more efficient and effective predictions.
ai.problemSolved: Optimizing resource allocation in complex machine learning models by dynamically selecting the most appropriate sub-models for different inputs.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves training individual models and gating networks. The architecture itself is software-based, requiring no physical components beyond computing resources.
ai.buildProcess: Models are trained independently on subsets of data or specific tasks. A gating network is then trained to predict which model should be used for each input based on its characteristics. This process can be automated using machine learning frameworks and libraries.
ai.costDrivers: Training costs, computational infrastructure, and the complexity of implementing effective gating networks. The cost of specialized hardware can also impact the build process.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The MoE architecture is expected to gain broader adoption as it offers significant benefits in terms of efficiency and performance across various applications.
ai.regulation: Currently, there are no specific regulations targeting MoE architectures. However, compliance with general data protection and privacy laws will be necessary depending on the application domain.
ai.risks: Overfitting to the gating network, potential bias in model selection, and computational overhead during inference can pose risks if not properly managed.
ai.profitability: The profitability of MoE architectures depends on their successful implementation across industries where efficient resource allocation is critical. Potential cost savings from reduced computation could drive adoption.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may focus on improving the efficiency of gating networks, integrating more diverse model types, and enhancing interpretability for better trust in decision-making processes.

glossary.def: A machine learning framework that combines multiple specialized models to improve overall performance and efficiency.
A neural network component in the MoE architecture responsible for selecting which sub-models should contribute to the final prediction based on input characteristics.

subsystems.name: Expert networks
subsystems.role: provide specialized computation; each expert is a separate feed-forward sub-network.

subsystems.name: Gating network (router)
subsystems.role: scores each token and selects which experts should process it.

subsystems.name: Token dispatch and combine
subsystems.role: sends tokens to their chosen experts and merges the results.

subsystems.name: Load balancing
subsystems.role: keeps experts evenly utilized so no expert dominates or starves.

subsystems.name: Distributed execution
subsystems.role: shards experts across many accelerators for training and inference.

buildSteps.title: Design the base model
buildSteps.detail: Start with a transformer and replace some feed-forward blocks with mixture-of-experts layers, leaving attention and normalization in place.

buildSteps.title: Choose expert count and routing budget
buildSteps.detail: Decide how many experts to create (for example, 8 or 64) and how many each token may use (for example, top-2).

buildSteps.title: Implement the router
buildSteps.detail: Build a small network that computes an affinity score between each token and each expert, then picks the highest-scoring ones.

buildSteps.title: Implement dispatch
buildSteps.detail: Group tokens by their chosen experts and send them to the devices holding those experts, then return the outputs.

buildSteps.title: Add load balancing
buildSteps.detail: Introduce an auxiliary loss that penalizes uneven expert usage and a capacity factor that caps tokens per expert per batch.

buildSteps.title: Train at scale
buildSteps.detail: Train on a large text or multimodal dataset using distributed hardware, with experts spread across accelerators.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate and tune
buildSteps.detail: Measure model quality, throughput and expert utilization; adjust routing, capacity and balancing weights.

buildSteps.title: Deploy for inference
buildSteps.detail: Run the trained model with expert sharding, dynamic batching and caching so only the selected experts compute for each token.

prerequisites.why: mixture-of-experts layers are most often inserted in place of feed-forward blocks.
experts must be split across many accelerators, requiring fast interconnects and parallelism.
tokens move between devices during routing, so communication can become the bottleneck.
without them, a few experts receive most tokens and the rest are wasted.
fast kernels are needed to execute only the selected experts without dense overhead.

pathway.milestone: sparse mixture-of-experts layers in large language models, typically routing each token to a small number of experts
pathway.unlocks: more parameters and knowledge at similar inference cost per token.

pathway.milestone: better routing and balancing methods that reduce wasted computation and improve stability
pathway.unlocks: larger expert counts and more reliable training.

pathway.milestone: mixture-of-experts for multimodal models with modality-specific experts
pathway.unlocks: one model that handles text, images and audio efficiently.

pathway.milestone: adaptive computation where routing varies with token difficulty, and hardware co-designed for expert parallelism
pathway.unlocks: further gains in efficiency and capability for very large models.
